entryAnswer.explanation:
The handoff is a validate-then-deliver function. `assertCausalCapabilities(graph, capability, expected)` is the only admission gate: it looks the object up in the module-private `issued` WeakMap and throws `TypeError("causal capability binding mismatch")` when the object was never issued (a structural copy or cast), when `root.graph !== graph`, when `root.level !== "full"`, or when contract/implementationRevision/scope/epoch differ from the expected binding (packages/ts/src/solutions/causal-occurrence/capabilities.ts:66-82). It then throws `TypeError("causal capability lineage mismatch")` unless each of `identity`, `execution`, `retained` is itself an issued handle of the same instance and Graph (capabilities.ts:83-87), and `TypeError("causal capability lower handle mismatch")` unless `execution.identity === identity` and `retained.execution === execution` (capabilities.ts:88-89). Because the assertion runs before `recipient(...)`, a structural copy, a different-Graph capability or a wrong binding never reaches the recipient; the README states the same rule: "A capability validation failure must be handled before passing the capabilities to a recipient; a structural copy is not an issued object" (examples/spending-alerts/README.md:41-43).

Delivery preserves identity relationships by passing the original frozen handles, not copies: `createCausalCapabilities` builds `identity`, `execution` (with `identity` nested), `retained` (with `execution` nested) and `full` as frozen objects and registers each level in the WeakMap (capabilities.ts:122-147). The demo asserts exactly these relationships after handoff: `execution === app.capabilities.execution`, `execution.identity === app.capabilities.identity`, `app.capabilities.retained.execution === execution` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-graded-demo.ts:85-87), and the framework example returns `capabilities.execution` unchanged after validation (examples/spending-alerts/causal-audience.examples.ts:17-25). The binding itself is validated/normalized by `causalBinding` (capabilities.ts:53-64), and the preset constructs the expected binding with `contract: "contract-v2"`, `implementationRevision: "construction-v1"`, `scope: "full"`, `epoch: binding.compositionEpoch` (examples/spending-alerts/causal-preset.ts:114-119).

Possession of the execution level does NOT authorize an arbitrary I/O call. `ExecutionCapability` exposes only graph Nodes (`terminals`, `conservation`, `causalQuiescence`) plus the identity handles (capabilities.ts:27-32); there is no write/open/execute method. The README says "Capabilities have no arbitrary I/O execution method" (README.md:94), and the audience example comments "an execution view grants no I/O method" (causal-audience.examples.ts:17). Actual I/O is gated elsewhere: the resource lease must be `transferred` before `write` is allowed (examples/spending-alerts/causal-resource.ts:76-79), and admission requires a matching local grant, current policy watermark, and ready inbox slot (examples/spending-alerts/causal-admission.ts:253-296). So the execution level is an observation/lineage handle, not an authorization token; a name or handle is not permission (README.md:86, 122-123).
